name: sysctl
description: Reads and changes kernel runtime parameters exposed under /proc/sys — networking buffers, swappiness, limits, and more.

flags.description: Read one parameter (dots map to /proc/sys/ paths).
Set a parameter at runtime (lost at reboot).
Load settings from all standard locations.

examples.explanation: How eagerly the kernel swaps (0 = avoid, 100 = aggressive).
Enables IP forwarding immediately — required for routers, VPNs, and Docker NAT setups.
The persistent way: a file in /etc/sysctl.d/ plus loading it.
System-wide open file limit — relevant for high-connection servers.

about: Every file under /proc/sys/ is a tunable kernel parameter; sysctl is just a friendly interface to reading/writing them. Runtime changes (-w) vanish at reboot — persistence lives in /etc/sysctl.conf or /etc/sysctl.d/*.conf. Some parameters (e.g. certain network settings) only take effect safely in specific states; document changes.
mistakes: Setting parameters with -w and wondering why they reset at reboot.
Copying random tuning guides without understanding the parameters.
warnings: Kernel tunables can destabilize or open security holes (e.g. ip_forward on a multi-tenant host). Change one at a time and verify.
